Idiom (Gwari): Etsu be ganya, ma ganya yi na be
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed biclausal equative-negation proverb; parallel noun phrases linked through contrastive repetition.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Authority without wisdom is empty: a person is not a legitimate leader merely because they hold a title.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: A leader must be wise to deserve recognition as a leader.
Usage Contexts: Traditional leadership; politics; community deliberation; family counsel; moral instruction
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested in a study of male-oriented Gbagyi proverbs under leadership and authority. It reflects the customary expectation that an etsu should govern through judgment, responsibility, and service rather than status alone.
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Gwari): /ét͡sù bè ɡàɲá | mà ɡàɲá jì ná bè/
First Example Sentence: Etsu be ganya, ma ganya yi na be.
Second Example Sentence: Etsu be ganya—ma ganya yi na be!
Third Example Sentence: Baba gwi, eshuka be; etsu be ganya, ma ganya yi na be.

Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: A father’s considered words carry lasting authority and should not be dismissed casually.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: A responsible father’s advice deserves serious attention.
Usage Contexts: Family meetings; elder–youth counsel; dispute settlement; moral teaching

Idiom (Gwari): Ba eyi nu gaga, ba pe yi nu giwa
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed parallel comparative construction; negative human description matched to a tree-without-roots image.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: A person lacking inner strength, stability, or resolve is vulnerable and cannot flourish under pressure.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: A person needs resilience and a firm foundation to withstand hardship.
Usage Contexts: Advice; hardship; personal development; family responsibility; storytelling
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested in Gbagyi proverb analysis using the rooted tree as an ecological metaphor. Farming and woodland imagery make rootedness a culturally intelligible model for stability, nourishment, and survival.
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Gwari): /bà èjì nù ɡàɡà | bà pè jì nù ɡìwà/
First Example Sentence: Ba eyi nu gaga, ba pe yi nu giwa.
Second Example Sentence: Ba eyi nu gaga—ba pe yi nu giwa!
Third Example Sentence: Ka ba gwi, a ba gwi yi ra; ba eyi nu gaga, ba pe yi nu giwa.

Idiom (Gwari): Gwagwa shi be, a du yi shi gwi
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed negative declarative proverb; agent noun followed by a negated flight/retreat predicate and battlefield complement.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: A courageous person does not abandon a serious responsibility merely because danger or difficulty appears.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Face difficult responsibilities with courage instead of running away.
Usage Contexts: Conflict; work; communal duty; encouragement; political rhetoric
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested as a Gbagyi warrior metaphor. It recalls the social prestige attached to bravery, communal defence, persistence, and remaining present when collective responsibilities become difficult.
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Gwari): /ɡʷàɡʷà ʃì bè | à dù jì ʃì ɡʷì/
First Example Sentence: Gwagwa shi be, a du yi shi gwi.
Second Example Sentence: Gwagwa shi be—a du yi shi gwi!
Third Example Sentence: Gara yi tsu tsu, a kwi yi dan; gwagwa shi be, a du yi shi gwi.

Idiom (Gwari): Gara yi tsu tsu, a kwi yi dan
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed contrastive negative clause; strong-person topic followed by a predicate denying fear of a heavy load.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Real strength is shown by accepting and carrying difficult responsibilities without intimidation.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: A resilient person accepts difficult responsibilities.
Usage Contexts: Workplace; farming; family provision; encouragement; rites of responsibility
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested in Gbagyi resilience discourse. The load metaphor draws on everyday labour, farming, carrying, and household obligation, extending physical burden to emotional and social responsibility.
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Gwari): /ɡàrà jì t͡sù t͡sù | à kʷì jì dàn/
First Example Sentence: Gara yi tsu tsu, a kwi yi dan.
Second Example Sentence: Gara yi tsu tsu—a kwi yi dan!
Third Example Sentence: Ba yi ganya, ba yi tso; gara yi tsu tsu, a kwi yi dan.

Idiom (Gwari): Ba zai, ba sa yi shi, lafi yi shi
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed conditional-like negative comparison; a person’s failure to defend a right is equated metaphorically with a toothless lion.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Someone who never asserts legitimate rights loses practical power, dignity, and the ability to resist mistreatment.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Defend your legitimate rights firmly and responsibly.
Usage Contexts: Justice; politics; labour relations; family disputes; civic speech
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested in a Gbagyi proverb study using a lion’s teeth as a symbol of effective agency. The image encodes courage and self-defence, not indiscriminate aggression.
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Gwari): /bà zàj | bà sà jì ʃì | làfì jì ʃì/
First Example Sentence: Ba zai, ba sa yi shi, lafi yi shi.
Second Example Sentence: Ba zai—ba sa yi shi, lafi yi shi!
Third Example Sentence: Gwagwa shi be, a du yi shi gwi; ba zai, ba sa yi shi, lafi yi shi.

Idiom (Gwari): Ka ba gwi, a ba gwi yi ra
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed simile-like parallel clause; steadfast human stance aligned with a tree remaining upright in a storm.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: A resolute person remains stable and committed despite adversity, opposition, or fear.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Remain firm and do not abandon a sound course because of pressure.
Usage Contexts: Encouragement; crisis; leadership; family counsel; public speaking
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested in Gbagyi resilience discourse. The tree-and-storm image reflects close observation of the natural environment and treats endurance as rooted steadiness rather than loud display.
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Gwari): /kà bà ɡʷì | à bà ɡʷì jì rà/
First Example Sentence: Ka ba gwi, a ba gwi yi ra.
Second Example Sentence: Ka ba gwi—a ba gwi yi ra!
Third Example Sentence: Ba eyi nu gaga, ba pe yi nu giwa; ka ba gwi, a ba gwi yi ra.

Idiom (Gwari): Ba yi ganya, ba yi tso
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed balanced negative construction; repeated subject–predicate frame establishes a necessary-condition relation.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Without resilience and sustained effort, a person cannot make meaningful progress.
Usage Contexts: Daily advice; education; work; farming; entrepreneurship; encouragement
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested in a Gbagyi study under resilience and endurance. It condenses a widely valued ethic of sustained labour and patience in the face of setbacks.
First Example Sentence: Ba yi ganya, ba yi tso.
Third Example Sentence: Yi yi fani, yi yi gba; ba yi ganya, ba yi tso.

Idiom (Gwari): Yi yi fani, yi yi gba
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed parallel clause with repeated subject marking; balanced predicates form an evaluative maxim.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: A person’s character is revealed less by easy beginnings than by the capacity to endure and overcome hardship.
Non-Idiomatic Equivalent (Plain, Neutral: Judge strength of character by sustained endurance.
Usage Contexts: Moral education; hardship; work; family counsel; ceremonial speech
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested in Gbagyi endurance discourse. The balanced form gives the saying mnemonic force and reflects oral teaching practices in which character is assessed through conduct over time.
First Example Sentence: Yi yi fani, yi yi gba.
Third Example Sentence: Gara yi tsu tsu, a kwi yi dan; yi yi fani, yi yi gba.

Idiom (Gwari): Ba yi tso, ba yi yi se
Syntactic Structure & Grammatical Form: Fixed cause–result maxim expressed through two balanced clauses; endurance is presented as the condition for success.
Figurative Meaning (Contextualized Defin: Success usually comes through persistence rather than immediate results.
Usage Contexts: Education; farming; work; business; family encouragement; youth mentoring
Cultural Origin or Historical Reference: Attested in Gbagyi proverb analysis under resilience and endurance. The saying reflects the practical experience that cultivation, craft, household provision, and communal achievement require patient continuity.
Phonetic Transcription (IPA, Gwari): /bà jì t͡sò | bà jì jì sè/
First Example Sentence: Ba yi tso, ba yi yi se.
Second Example Sentence: Ba yi tso—ba yi yi se!
Third Example Sentence: Ba yi ganya, ba yi tso; ba yi tso, ba yi yi se.
